interface.name: df_shell

description.summary: chrome-surface factory for trusted session clients

interface.description: Creates `df_layer_surface`s. Binding this global requires a successful `df_core.authenticate` (T-07 trust model).

request.name: get_layer_surface

description.summary: create a chrome surface on a layer

request.description: Turn an existing `wl_surface` into a chrome surface. The compositor assigns it a reserved zone (when `exclusive_zone` is set) and places it on the requested layer. `output` NULL targets **every** output (matching `wlr-layer-shell`'s all-output rule), so the menu bar and Dock anchor on any display attached later; a non-NULL output pins the surface to that one display, and its reserve applies only there (T-16.1a).

enum.name: layer
enum.description: Matches wlr-layer-shell's ordering so the mental model carries over: the wallpaper/desktop reveal sits on `background`, normal chrome on `top`, transient chrome (menus, OSD) on `overlay`.

interface.name: df_layer_surface
interface.description: Requests may be sent before the first commit; the compositor sends a `configure` with the resolved size and serial, which the client must ack. When the output is resized the compositor reconfigures.

description.summary: anchor edges; 0 means centred on the output

request.name: set_size
request.description: A non-zero width/height is a request, not a guarantee: the compositor may clamp it to the output and reports the final size in `configure`.

request.name: set_exclusive_zone

description.summary: reserve this many pixels on the anchored edge

request.description: The reserved zone is subtracted from the usable area (Zoom target) and reported to the shell as an output property. Negative values keep the surface out of the reserved-zone accounting (an overlay).

request.name: set_keyboard_interaction

description.summary: keyboard focus policy for this surface

request.description: `none` never takes keyboard focus; `on_demand` takes it when clicked; `exclusive` takes it for as long as it is mapped (like a modal OSD).

request.name: set_panel_rect

description.summary: declare the live rect the surface actually paints

request.description: The visible panel the backdrop material (T-04.2) belongs behind, in surface-local logical coordinates. A chrome surface whose painted area changes frame to frame — the Dock's plate grows to wrap magnified icons — sends its live rect here so the compositor's frosted backdrop follows it exactly. This state takes effect on the next wl_surface commit, together with the pixels it describes. The compositor intersects the rect with the surface geometry. An empty rectangle disables the backdrop. When unset, the compositor derives the panel from the input region and the reserved strip.

request.name: set_panel_region

description.summary: declare one independently keyed material region

request.description:
Adds or replaces one material region on this chrome surface, in surface-local logical coordinates. A surface may declare a bounded set of regions (currently eight) so one overlay can compose several detached cards, or a menu with square attached top corners and rounded bottom corners, without changing its input region or reserved zone.
`key` is a short stable token unique within the surface. `preset` is an optional known glass preset name; empty derives the preset from the surface namespace/role. `overscan` is extra visual reach for rim, shadow or veil beyond the visual rect. The four radii clip the region's corners independently.
Region requests are commit-latched with the pixels they describe. The first request after a commit starts from the committed list, so a single region can be added or replaced without resending its siblings; `clear_panel_regions` starts an explicitly empty list. Invalid keys, unknown presets, or a region beyond the bound are ignored, leaving the committed list intact. A client that only sends `set_panel_rect` keeps the legacy single-rect behavior.

request.name: clear_panel_regions

description.summary: commit an empty material region set

request.description: Replaces the committed region list with an empty list on the next `wl_surface.commit`. The surface keeps its input region and reserved zone; it simply draws no compositor material. Sending region requests after this call before the commit rebuilds a non-empty list.

request.name: set_auto_hide
request.description: Applies to the `menubar` surface only; other namespaces ignore it. The compositor owns the revealed state on each output. `never` keeps the bar visible in the desktop and in fullscreen. `always` starts concealed and reveals it from the top edge or the menu-bar focus shortcut. `full_screen` shows the bar normally on the desktop and conceals it in fullscreen until it is revealed. A concealed bar contributes no reserved zone, input hit area, or material panel, so the output stays eligible for direct scanout. A revealed bar keeps its normal reservation, input region, and material until it conceals again; an active menu or keyboard focus keeps it revealed.

description.summary: the compositor will not use this surface any more
